From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + MSA/DPA draft for redlines and timeline

Hannah / Vanessa —

Attaching our annotated redlines. High-level summary (quick hits):

1) Data residency & subprocessors
   - Equinox requests global processing. We will propose a carve that requires customer-specific residency controls for regulated customers (EU/UK). Request: explicit SOW clause for customer-by-customer residency requirements.

2) Audit & security assessment
   - Limit audit to SOC/SIEM evidence plus one on-site per 24 months with reasonable notice. Remove open-ended "any audit" language; define escalation path.

3) Liability cap and indemnity
   - Their standard liability cap is 3x fees or $5M (whichever is greater). We recommend capping at 3x fees up to $10M for strategic integrations and keeping exceptions limited to gross negligence/willful misconduct.

4) Data Processing Addendum (DPA)
   - Several clauses need tightening around subprocessors, data export, and deletion timelines. Recommend 30 days for delete confirmation post-termination and stronger obligations on subprocessors.

5) Termination & transitional support
   - Add 60-day transition support with limited access for data export; scope to be defined in SOW.

6) SOW clarity
   - Define integration milestones, acceptance criteria, and who owns customer support for the joint customers. Include an SLA table: availability, response targets, and escalation owners.

Attachments: Redwood_Equinox_MSA_redlines.docx (docx); DataProcessing_Addendum_comments.pdf (pdf)

Next steps: I’ll merge comments into a single file and share a link to the Drive. If Equinox is comfortable, propose a 30-minute legal call (we can do Wed or Thu mornings PST) to triage the biggest items (liability, audit, residency). If we don’t agree on those, we won’t block pricing/procurement but we will need exec alignment.

Markus — flagged you for any unusual infra/ops asks (residency/keys).

— Sergio
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Paula Jenkins <paula.jenkins@equinox-int.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Malhotra <amit@equinox-int.com>, Equinox Legal <legal@equinox-int.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intro + MSA/DPA draft for redlines and timeline

Sergio / Hannah —

Thanks for the thorough summary. A few immediate positions from Equinox Legal:

- Liability cap: we can consider a banded approach tied to ARR for strategic partnerships, but a $10M cap is likely above what our procurement will accept for an initial integration. Propose meet-in-the-middle: 3x fees up to $7.5M.
- Audit: acceptable to limit on-site audits to once per 24 months, but we need to keep "reasonable scope" language that covers joint customer investigations.
- Data residency: we can accept SOW-specific residency restrictions; however, we need a standard fallback that permits global processing unless otherwise specified.

We’re generally happy to move forward with a legal call tomorrow (Wed) at 10:00 AM PST. We’ll have our procurement lead on the call to confirm PO vs Net30 and to outline the typical onboarding cadence.

If you can share the consolidated redlines doc + a short one-pager with the non-starters and negotiables before the call, that will help speed things up.

Paula
General Counsel, Equinox Integrations
paula.jenkins@equinox-int.com
